scope: Optimized emitted code on the pinned PAL machine, nominal 57.6k SDFS. Matched disabled/idle/two-active-client panels and raw-event pointer fixtures; original AS0 tolerances unchanged. Current final source was held fixed while all late-* images were built. No demo refresh or release/hardware qualification.
changes: Use copied widget action epoch/revision/state for status patches; snapshot only for loss/stale recovery. Keep full transactional validation and context capacities.
Copy only active widget objects/text for updates; damage title/focus underline instead of entire non-console client on focus.
Read clock through checked snapshot without timer queue edit gate; equivalent smaller PAL/NTSC deadline arithmetic.
Single event-client scan, lazy fresh clock, skip inactive Wake; match expiries again after native output before yielding.
Reserve one shared AES admission after a ready paint/input quantum; at most three native plus one AES admission on that turn.
One bounded native-control opportunity after paint releases scene, before a new console writer takes it.

limits.scope: Compare matched optimized configurations and workloads: 10 gestures per widget cohort and 30 pointer motions/button edges. Development measurements, not qualification.
limits.explanation: 20.1 ms allows one PAL scanout-observation frame of phase difference. CPU/consumption budgets are explicit integration allowances, not measured jitter. No deliberate extra-frame wait is allowed. Exceedances require investigation before AS4 acceptance.

comparison.scope: Loaded allowance applies when either GEM clients or native scroll/disk work is active. Both frozen AS0 and matched AES-disabled comparisons are retained. Combined visibility includes the sequential label-observation upper bound.

latency.scope: Passive emitted boundaries; reply means public ReplyMsg invocation. Client means checked binding epilogue. Standalone timer calls only in device-to-AES distribution; VBI rounding excluded from deadline latency.

removed_experiments: Additional callbacks inside event matching worsened the pointer consumption tail.
Yielding immediately after a widget action shortened commit-to-patch time but worsened visible button feedback.
diagnostics.retained_ordering: Moving the reserved AES admission after the paint quantum preserved bounded progress and improved the loaded panel cohort; raw pointer consumption still misses the relative limit.
test_repairs: Four-client clock-fault injection now explicitly waits for four admissions before matching, preserving the message recovery assertions.
Alarm transport fixture controller stage is runnable work even without an application event wait.
Passive patch marker is associated with the model commit, not the later sampled application receipt; SetTree/full-redraw comparison does not require a WidgetUpdate marker.
diagnostics.observer_scope: Patch benchmark uses event state; matched full-tree replacement reads the states it must preserve. Final scene still has an independent pixel oracle. Completed-scanout before/after checks are not a continuous whole-gesture flicker proof.

conclusion: Native disabled panel/pointer regressions pass the frozen comparison. AES disabled/idle/loaded functional checks pass. Active pointer visibility improves from 106.53 to 46.66 ms p95, but consumption and matched complete-feedback limits remain open. AS4 and timer TD4 are not accepted. Existing absolute widget and 125k transport goals remain open.
